description:
Found s504 by s501t (t/op/avhv.t probes).  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main b7ec0093 and for an UNTIED array (not a tie question).

Reproducer (perl: every line `[Not a HASH reference ...]`):
    my $a = [1];
    eval { my @k = keys %$a };  print "4 [$@]\n";   # PCL: 4 []        (silent: keys of an ARRAY ref through %$)
    eval { $a->{x}{y} = 1 };    print "5 [$@]\n";   # PCL: The value #() is not of type hash-table
    eval { $a->{q}[0] = 1 };    print "9 [$@]\n";   # PCL: same raw CL type error
The single-level forms (`$a->{k} = 1`, `exists`, `delete`, slices, `%$a = LIST`) die perl's way.  Two sites: p-cast-% on an array referent (keys/values/each read it as a container) and the autoviv chain (expand-autoviv / p-autoviv-set) reaching gethash with a vector.  Rule 12 / "errors fail in the same places as perl and are TIDY" (USER).  Layer: runtime, the %p-wrong-referent-p predicate the single-level paths already use.
subject: `keys %$aref` does not die "Not a HASH reference", and `$aref->{k}{x} = 1` / `$aref->{k}[0] = 1` die with a raw CL type error (`The value #() is not of type hash-table`) instead of perl's message
